words.meaning: unable to keep still or silent, impatient

words.meaning: free from disturbance

words.meaning: the action of keeping careful watch for danger

words.meaning: an area of land, especially farmland

words.meaning: made a feeling or belief disappear

words.meaning: the state of not being serious or sensible

words.meaning: the quality of being impossible to understand or enter

words.meaning: not merciful or gentle, giving freely

words.meaning: the state of using too many words

words.meaning: the state of spending resources freely and recklessly

words.meaning: the quality of saying very little

words.meaning: the quality of speaking fluently and incessantly

words.meaning: the quality of being transparently clear

words.meaning: to support or strengthen

words.meaning: of minor relevance, on the edge

words.meaning: the state of avoiding the company of others

words.meaning: expressing feelings in an unrestrained manner

words.meaning: having become accustomed to something unpleasant

words.meaning: to make more lively or interesting

words.meaning: to set the boundaries or limits of something

words.meaning: long strips or areas of something

words.meaning: groups of people assembled for a purpose

words.meaning: pushed or thrust forward

words.meaning: unable to understand, bewildered

words.mnemonic: "patience-less-aunt" - My aunt who has very less patience gets 'irritated' over small-small things, and now that aunt will always remind me of this word!

words.meaning: worthy of high praise
words.example: To say that Gandhi's actions were laudable is the greatest understatement; he overthrew an empire without violence.
words.mnemonic: It feels and means like "applaud-able"!

words.meaning: intended to attract notice and impress others; tawdry or vulgar
words.example: Matt wanted to buy stone lions for front of the house, but Cynthia convinced him that such a display would be too ostentatious for a modest house in an unassuming neighborhood.
words.mnemonic: "ass-tempts-us" - It's kind of 'vulgar' when someone says - 'that ass is tempting'.

words.meaning: extreme generosity and giving
words.example: Uncle Frank was known for his largess, so his nephew was sad when he did not receive a present for his birthday.
words.mnemonic: "large-ness" - Someone with a large heart is 'very generous and giving'.

words.meaning: praise or glorify
words.example: The teenagers exalted the rock star, covering their bedrooms with posters of him.
words.mnemonic: "extra-salt" - I once 'praised' my friend for putting some extra salt in my food!

words.meaning: without any attempt at concealment; completely obvious
words.example: Allen was often punished in school for blatantly disrespecting teachers.
words.mnemonic: "blunt-aunt" - That blunt aunt 'blatantly' scolded me for parking my car in front of her house.

words.meaning: make one thing compatible with another
words.example: Peggy was unable to reconcile her kind friend Jane with the cruel and merciless character Jane played on television.
words.mnemonic: "re-counsel" - I had to re (again) counsel the couple in order to make them feel they both are 'compatible' with each other.

words.meaning: refusing to change one's mind
words.example: Civil rights icon Rosa Parks will forever be remembered for adamantly refusing to give up her seat on a public bus--even after the bus driver insisted, she remained rooted in place.
words.mnemonic: "a-dumb-man" - He is a dumb man who is 'refusing to accept' the fact that earth is round.

words.meaning: add details or explanation; clarify the meaning; state in depth
words.example: The CEO refused to expound on the decision to merge our department with another one, and so I quit.
words.mnemonic: It feels and means like "explain" and "expand".

words.meaning: a behavioral attribute that is distinctive and peculiar to an individual
words.example: Peggy's numerous idiosyncrasies include wearing mismatched shoes, laughing loudly to herself, and owning a pet aardvark.
words.mnemonic: It feels and means like "idiot-psycho- crazy".

words.meaning: reject as untrue or unfounded
words.example: Many in the public believed the rumors of a UFO crash outside town, so the chief of police did everything he could to repudiate the rumors.
words.mnemonic: "refuse that I ate" - I 'refused to accept' his allegation that I ate his burger.

words.meaning: assign great social importance to
words.example: Students in the U.S. learn to lionize Jefferson, Franklin, and Washington because they are the founding fathers of the nation.
words.mnemonic: "lion-size" - Lion sized people are given 'great social importance' in some countries.

words.meaning: restrict or confine
words.example: Their tour of South America was circumscribed so that they saw only popular destinations and avoided the dangerous parts of cities.
words.mnemonic: "circumference" - The circumference of the circle 'confines' the inside area of the circle.

words.meaning: feeling or showing profound respect or veneration
words.example: The professor could speak objectively about the other composers, but he always lectured about Brahms with a particularly reverent air, unable to offer a single criticism of his compositions.
words.mnemonic: "real-rent" - That landlord takes only the 'real rent' of the house so everyone 'respects' him.

words.meaning: fearless
words.example: Captain Ahab was an intrepid captain whose reckless and fearless style ultimately lead to his downfall.
words.mnemonic: "interrupt-sid" - He interrupted his boss Sid 'without any fear' of getting scolded.

words.meaning: intellectually productive
words.example: Schubert was the most prolific composer, producing hundreds of hours of music before he died at the age of 31.
words.mnemonic: "productive-life" - He is very 'intellectual' and hence living a 'productive' life.

words.meaning: exclude from a community or group
words.example: Later in his life, Leo Tolstoy was ostracized from the Russian Orthodox Church for his writings that contradicted church doctrine.
words.mnemonic: "extra-size" - Because of his extra size he was 'excluded from the community' of slim people.

words.meaning: marked by great carelessness; dependent upon or characterized by chance
words.example: Many golf courses are designed with great care, but the greens on the county golf course seem entirely haphazard.
words.mnemonic: "happened-hazard" - That hazard happened because of the great 'carelessness' of the people.

words.meaning: extremely hungry; devouring or craving food in great quantities
words.example: John didn't eat much at all during the week he had the flu, so now that he is regaining his health, it's not surprising that he has a ravenous appetite.
words.mnemonic: "Ravan" - Ravan was a king of Lanka (in ancient epic Ramayana) who was 'extremely hungry' for power, and now Ravan will help you remember this word!

words.meaning: a large indefinite number
words.example: There are a myriad of internet sites hawking pills that claim to boost energy for hours on end.
words.mnemonic: "Pyramid" - Pyramids have 'indefinite number' of steps, and now those steps won't let you forget this word!

words.meaning: dominance over a certain area
words.example: Until the Spanish Armada was defeated in 1587, Spain had hegemony over the seas, controlling waters stretching as far as the Americas.
words.mnemonic: "huge-money" - Huge amount of money always leads to 'dominance' over something.

words.meaning: hostile (usually describes conditions or environments)
words.example: Venus, with a surface temperature that would turn rubber to liquid, is inimical to any form of life.
words.mnemonic: "enemy-call" - When an enemy calls it creates a 'hostile environment', and now your enemies will always remind of this word!

words.meaning: cancel officially
words.example: The man's driver's license was rescinded after his tenth car accident, which meant he would never be allowed to legally drive again.
words.mnemonic: "resign" - It's like when I resigned, my job got 'cancelled officially', and now this resignation will help you remember this word!

words.meaning: readily reacting to suggestions and influences; easily managed (controlled or taught or molded)
words.example: Compared to middle school students, who have an untamed wildness about them, high school students are somewhat more tractable.
words.mnemonic: "track-table" - I was 'tracking' all the suggestions that were being provided on that round 'table' conference and 'reacting actively' on them.

words.meaning: disturb in mind or cause to be worried or alarmed
words.example: Now that Henry is recovering from a major illness, he no longer lets the little trivialities, such as late mail, perturb him.
words.mnemonic: It feels and means like "disturb"!

words.meaning: in a blunt, direct manner
words.example: Not one for social pleasantries, the Chief of Staff would brusquely ask his subordinates anything he wanted, even coffee.
words.mnemonic: "bruises" - Associate it with some 'bruises' that you might have got from 'blunt' surfaces, so that those bruises don't let you forget this word!

words.meaning: use of physical or mental energy; hard work; agony or anguish
words.example: While they experienced nothing but travails in refinishing the kitchen, they completed the master bedroom in less than a weekend.
words.mnemonic: "travel - all" - You will have to 'use a lot of physical energy', in case you decide to travel the whole world, and now this world trip won't let you forget this word!

words.meaning: tendency to believe readily
words.example: Virginia's wide-eyed credulity as a five-year old was replaced by suspicion after she learned that Santa Claus didn't really exist.
words.mnemonic: "credibility" - You 'tend to believe' someone easily who has good 'credibility', and now those credible people won't let you forget this word!

words.meaning: close in time; about to occur
words.example: The impending doom of our world has been discussed and debated for 2000 years, maybe even longer.
words.mnemonic: It feels and means like "i'm pending"!

words.meaning: to make a witty remark, to say in jest; a witty saying
words.example: When an old English teacher criticized Churchill for ending a sentence with a preposition, he quipped, "This is the kind of criticism up with which we will not put!"
words.mnemonic: "quick-wit" - It's like you 'quip' when you make a 'quick witty' remark, and now that witty remark will help you remember this word!

words.meaning: marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable
words.example: A good captain needs to be steadfast, continuing to hold the wheel and stay the course even during the most violent storm.
words.mnemonic: It feels and means like "steady and fast" i.e. not shakable and determined to achieve something quickly!

words.meaning: make dirty or spotty, as by exposure to air; also used metaphorically
words.example: Pete Rose was one of the best baseball players of his generation, but his involvement with gambling on baseball games has tarnished his image in the eyes of many.
words.mnemonic: "tar-nish" - Tar is a rough and dirty substance, so 'tarnish' can be remembered as 'making something dirty'.

words.meaning: lack of agreement or harmony
words.example: Despite all their talented players, the team was filled with discord--some players refused to talk to others--and lost most of their games.
words.mnemonic: "dis-cord" - Absence of a 'cord' (i.e. connecting line or connection that ensures harmony) can lead to confusion and disconnect, and now that cord will help you remember this word!

words.meaning: a clever plan to turn a situation to one's advantage
words.example: Dennis arranged an elaborate ploy, involving 14 different people lying for him in different situations, so that it could appear that he was meeting Mary completely by chance at the wedding reception.
words.mnemonic: It feels and means like "plot".

words.meaning: urge on with unpleasant comments
words.example: Doug did not want to enter the race, but Jim, through a steady stream of taunts, goaded him into signing up for it.
words.mnemonic: "GO and Do (it)" - If you imagine a scene in which someone is telling you 'Go and Do it' unpleasantly, then you will never forget this word!

words.meaning: irritate or vex
words.example: My little sister has a way of irking and annoying me like no other person.
words.mnemonic: "jerk" - You must have called someone 'jerk' who 'irritated' or troubled you, and now that jerk won't let you forget this word!

words.meaning: pull inward or towards a center; formally reject or disavow a formerly held belief, usually under pressure
words.example: Email is wonderfully efficient, but once something awkward or damaging has been sent, there is no way to retract it.
words.mnemonic: "re-track" - If you 'track back' your steps and move back the path that you had earlier taken, then you will never forget this word!

words.meaning: wishing or appearing to wish evil to others; arising from intense ill will or hatred
words.example: Villains are known for their malevolent nature, oftentimes inflicting cruelty on others just for enjoyment.
words.mnemonic: "male-violent" - Some people are very violent and evil who always 'think of harming others', and now those kind of people won't let you forget this word!

words.meaning: be characteristic of; clarify by giving an example of
words.example: Lincoln exemplified the best of not only America, but also the potential greatness that exists within each person.
words.mnemonic: It feels and means like "example-clarify"!

words.meaning: use to the limit; exhaust
words.example: The hike to the summit of Mt. Whitney was so taxing that I could barely speak or stand up.
words.mnemonic: "Taxes" are just "exhausting" my pocket, so till I am paying my taxes I just can't forget this word!

words.meaning: make more attractive by adding ornament, colour, etc.; make more beautiful
words.example: McCartney would write relatively straightforward lyrics, and Lennon would embellish them with puns and poetic images.
words.mnemonic: "emblem-ish" - Emblems are intricately beautiful designs or badges that symbolize something, so it's like you 'embellish' something by adding a beautiful emblem.

words.meaning: easily irritated or annoyed
words.example: Our office manager is peevish, so the rest of us tip-toe around him, hoping not to set off another one of his fits.
words.mnemonic: "pee-wish" - When I feel like peeing and I don't find a washroom nearby, then I start getting 'irritated' and 'annoyed'.

words.meaning: characterized by care and perseverance in carrying out tasks
words.example: Michael was a diligent gardener, never leaving a leaf on the ground and regularly watering each plant.
words.mnemonic: "daily-intelligent" - If you start using 'intelligence' for your daily 'tasks', then you will never forget this word!

words.meaning: a state of deep-seated ill-will
words.example: The rude remark Charles made toward Sarah yesterday was due to his illness, not due to any real enmity toward Sarah.
words.mnemonic: "enemy" - We always have 'enmity' or 'ill-will' towards our 'enemy'.

words.meaning: taking part in immoral and unethical plots
words.example: With the help of the prince, the queen connived to overthrow the king.
words.mnemonic: "con-knife" - If you see a con (or convict) with a knife in his hands then you know that he is up to some crime or unethical activity, and now that con will not let you forget this word!

words.meaning: not normal
words.example: According to those who do not believe in climate change, the extreme weather over the last five years is simply anomalous, daily temperatures should return to their old averages, they believe.
words.mnemonic: It's like pronouncing "ab-normal" with b silent!

words.meaning: to reprimand harshly
words.example: Drill sergeants are known to castigate new recruits so mercilessly that the latter often break down during their first week in training.
words.mnemonic: "caste-gate" - A 'casteist' showed me the 'gate' (door) because I belonged to a different caste, which felt and meant like 'castigate'.

words.meaning: the condition of being susceptible to bribes or corruption
words.example: Even some of the most sacred sporting events are not immune to venality, as many of the officials have received substantial bribes to make biased calls.
words.mnemonic: "penalty" - 'Venality' will make your way to 'penalty' and that 'way' will not let you forget this word!

words.meaning: to sap energy from
words.example: John preferred to avoid equatorial countries; the intense sun would always leave him enervated after he'd spent the day sightseeing.
words.mnemonic: It feels and means like "energy evaporate"!

words.meaning: lacking
words.example: She did not think her vocabulary was wanting, yet there were so many words that inevitably she found a few she didn't know.
words.mnemonic: I "want" what I "lack"!... and the thing that I lack won't let me forget this word!

words.meaning: shapeless
words.example: His study plan for the GRE was at best amorphous; he would do questions from random pages in any one of seven test prep books.
words.mnemonic: "a-morphed-us" - A 'morphed' photo of 'us' can make our life 'shapeless'.

words.meaning: to be naive and innocent
words.example: Two-years in Manhattan had changed Jenna from an ingenuous girl from the suburbs to a jaded urbanite, unlikely to fall for any ruse, regardless of how elaborate.
words.mnemonic: "in-generous" - In generous people we can find 'ingenuous' or 'innocent' soul!

words.meaning: to be likely to socialize with others
words.example: Often we think that great leaders are those who are gregarious, always in the middle of a large group of people; yet, as Mahatma Gandhi and many others have shown us, leaders can also be introverted.
words.mnemonic: "gorgeous" - I like to 'socialize' with gorgeous people and this habit of mine won't let me forget this word!

words.meaning: a long pompous speech; a tirade; to deliver a long pompous speech or tirade
words.example: Dinner at Billy's was more a punishment than a reward, since anyone who sat at the dinner table would have to listen to Billy's father's interminable harangues against the government.
words.mnemonic: "harass" - Whenever I go late to office my boss harasses me by giving a 'long speech', and that harassment can never let me forget this word.

words.meaning: mixed or conflicting emotions about something
words.example: Sam was ambivalent about studying for the exam because doing so ate up a lot of his time, yet he was able to improve his analytical skills.
words.mnemonic: "valent-ines day" - We generally get 'mixed emotions' on valentine's day, and hence those emotions will help us remember this word!

words.meaning: (describes a person, speech, or style of writing) using very few words
words.example: While Martha always swooned over the hunky, laconic types in romantic comedies, her boyfriends inevitably were very talkative and not very hunky.
words.mnemonic: "lack-on-ink" - Since my pen lacked on ink, so I had to write the exam 'using very few words'.

words.meaning: being disrespectful; improperly forward or bold
words.example: Dexter, distraught over losing his pet dachshund, Madeline, found the police officer's questions impertinent, after all, he thought, did she have to pry into such details as to what Madeline's favorite snack was?
words.mnemonic: "improper-aunt" - One improper aunt in my neighbourhood is so 'disrespectful' that she will never let me forget this word all my life!

words.meaning: to reproach; to scold
words.example: Bob took a risk walking into the "Students' Barbershop", in the end he had to upbraid the apparently drunk barber for giving him an uneven bowl cut.
words.mnemonic: "up-bride" - The bridegroom upbraided (scolded) the horse when the horse threw his 'bride' 'up' from the carriage! This funny scene won't let you forget this word!

words.meaning: the power to foresee the future
words.example: Baxter's warnings about investing in technology stocks seemed like an act of prescience after the whole market declined significantly.
words.mnemonic: "priests-sense" - Some priests can sense 'what is going to happen next'. Those priests will always remind you the meaning of this word!

words.meaning: characteristic of rural life; awkwardly simple and provincial
words.example: The vacation cabin had no electricity and no indoor plumbing, but despite these inconveniences, Nigel adored its rustic charm.
words.mnemonic: "raw street" - We find 'raw' streets generally in 'rural areas', and those streets will help you remember this word!

words.meaning: habitually complaining
words.example: The querulous old woman was beginning to wear down even the happier members of the staff with her ceaseless complaining.
words.mnemonic: It feels and means like "quarrel-us"!

words.meaning: relevant and appropriate
words.example: The professor wanted to tell the jury in detail about his new book, but the lawyer said it wasn't germane to the charges in the cases.
words.mnemonic: German language is more 'germane' (relevant) in Germany!

words.meaning: criticize severely or angrily
words.example: Showing no patience, the manager utterly lambasted the sales team that lost the big account.
words.mnemonic: "I-am-bastard" - One of my friends angrily 'criticized' himself by shouting 'I am bastard' when he was 'very angry' on himself.

words.meaning: a strong liking
words.example: Monte had a predilection for the fine things in life: Cuban cigars, 200 dollar bottles of wine, and trips to the French Riviera.
words.mnemonic: "Pred-likes-one" - A boy named Pred 'likes' one girl a lot, and now that boy will always remind me of this word!
